review: Trouble Witches é pura diversão arcade em forma de shmup (jogo de navinha). Esqueça tramas complexas: aqui, o foco é a satisfação imediata. O grande trunfo do jogo é o viciante sistema de risco e recompensa: você ativa um círculo mágico para desacelerar as balas inimigas e, ao derrotar quem atirou, transforma todo aquele perigo em uma chuva de moedas de ouro. Esse dinheiro é usado para comprar feitiços caóticos e escudos em lojinhas no meio da fase, criando um ciclo de jogabilidade frenético e recompensador. Com uma estética anime super colorida, trilha sonora empolgante e várias bruxinhas únicas para jogar, é o tipo de jogo feito para quem quer desligar o cérebro, desviar de projéteis e ver a tela explodir em cores e moedas. Uma pérola vibrante e genuinamente divertida.

Confused yet? Well there's more. This particular version got an enhanced port on the PS4 which later got an enhanced port on the PS5. These versions were never released on PC but as I understand it the changes are redrawn HD graphics and all DLC characters included in the base game.
So, what do we get on this version?
The arcade version presented in glorious 4:3, the enhanced arcade version running in 16:9, the story mode which adds intro and ending cutscenes for each character along with interactions with the bosses, a challenge mode and Steam achievements.
On the technical side of things, the game is limited to 720p/60 (probably a remnant of the 360 port) with fullscreen and windowed options. The default audio mix makes the voices a bit hard to hear but it can be changed from the settings.
The localization needs ssome extra proofreading as it contains more grammatical errors than my reviews but I'll admit that it's pretty funny.

I mostly got this for the Cotton DLC. I own all the other Cotton games on Switch and Steam. I bought it during a sale when it was dirt cheap. But it is a really fun game. A great horizontal shooter with crazy weapons. It's one of those magical girl shmups.

This is an incredibly weak no recommend more based on what I like from a STG than how solid the game is itself. And I think Trouble Witches Origin - Episode 1 Daughters of Amalgam is well crafted. However, I like my shumps simple. I also of the ABS (Always Be Shooting) believe. Both things I just don't feel this game fosters. Among other issues I personally don't like. 

Playing this shump, I am always a bit confused on exactly how it works. I mean, there is a tutorial and everything. Part of the draw of shumps for me is the the pick-up-and-play, though. Not that I think this game is overly complicated. I just don't quite understand how it wants me to play.

There is some bullet canceling magic that I still haven't quite figured out. Because sometimes it just slows the enemy projectiles and sometimes it cancels them. Unless they are blue, which the cancel magic basically has no effect. The whole system throws off part of what I enjoy about shoot 'em ups: the dodging of projectiles. 

The game doesn't force the player to shot shooting. But it does if you want to collect enough money to buy decent upgrades at the shop. Which really does make the game much more managable and fun. As the player can buy card that allow for card that afford temporary powerful attacks of various types. That when activated also appear to generate more money to buy more upgrades when the shop floats by.  Which is not a game loop I particularly enjoy.

The stages themselves seem more challenging than the sub-bosses and stage bosses. If only because it is so easy to fall behind on your routing or hold back on using your magic bullet clearing powers. And for the most part, the bosses seem to have more uncancelable projectiles making them easier for me. Giving the whole game an odd feel that I both don't really know what I am doing, and I don't really feel like my maneuvering is all that important compared to knowing when to use my bullet cancel magic or spell card attacks. 

Leading to the whole game feeling like a confusing and unsatisfying experience. Combine that with being a cute-em'-up, which I don't like as much as even a generic spaceship shooter, means I don't really have much fun with this game as I do a whole host of other shoot 'em ups. But again, a lot of that is my own personal preference.

I think if I like something like Cotton more, I would probably like this game more. But if I am honest, I don't much like playing this game. It just does too much that is counter to what I like in shumps for me to enjoy. Even if it technically doesn't do anything wrong.

7/10  Fun game, but there are a few presentation / gameplay optimization issues.

The translation is quite bad, to the point that it's hard to tell what's going on in the story and the menus at times.  The game modes aren't really explained at all, anywhere, so it's up to you to figure out what the differences are between them, which is kinda hard since there are like 5 or 6 playable modes.

The most annoying issue to me is that the restart button on the pause menu only works in the Score Attack mode, which is weird since it's present but unusable in every other game mode.  This means you have to go all the way back thru the mode, character select, etc menus if you want to restart a stage / run.  Making this worse is the fact that the practice mode has a stage select, but not a section select, so you have to grind thru an entire stage over and over if you want to practice a tough section or boss, without being able to quick restart.

For a game with 10ish character dlc, each costing several dollars, I feel like the developers should take the time to polish and tighten the game a bit more.  Shipping a difficult bullethell with no quick restart shouldn't be acceptable.

Otherwise the game is fun and charming, with interesting mechanics and fast bullethell gameplay.  I wish I could grind the levels to try for 1cc, but the game is def fun for casual play.

Fun side scrolling danmaku. Sprites are large and well detailed and laid against generally pleasing backgrounds that contain both 2D and 3D elements. Some of the background 3D can appear a bit low res at times but it is not too much an issue overall. While the visuals are very good and well detailed on the whole, it is worth noting that the resolution is capped at 720p so while it looks fine on a 1080p display I imagine it could appear somewhat blurrier on higher resolution displays. 

The gameplay is tight and responsive with a surprisingly high degree of difficulty. Each of the characters have a general rapid shot and the ability to create a sphere around themselves that slows down enemy bullets and converts them into coins. The movement is a little fast and takes some adjustment as there is no focus button as far as I'm aware. There are spell cards that take the place of bombs, they vary in effect but most produce some offensive effect like a wave shot, a rain of fire balls, bubbles, a special rapid shot, and more. Enemies convert into coins that are automatically collected by the player when the spells are active. During normal gameplay the player must release the shot button for the coins to be absorbed.

All in all a fun and challenging side scrolling bullet hell.

Trouble Witches Origin is a shmup that really wants you to abuse the resources given to you.  Unlike other games where your special resources aka bombs or survival tools are very limited, this game actively wants you to keep spending the power ups you buy in the middle of a run via the shop mechanic you fly into mid-stages.  Between the mechanics of the magic barrier to slow most bullets down, the special power ups and the pretty wide range of characters with DLC including Cotton of Cotton fame, there's honestly a pretty hefty content package here to mess around with.  

A deceptively challenging game that increases in difficulty exponentially the further you get, it also feels super satisfying to keep pushing for that "one more run" feeling and dipping your toes into higher difficulties.  Challenge, engrish, goofy anime things: all of these things blended in the right amounts make for something that kinda surprised me with how fun it feels to play the more you get used to it.

One minus I can mention about the game is that leaderboards let you continue to keep your score going but at least still leave a number at the end of the score denoting how many credits were used at score submission when that run ended. Trouble Witches has 2 mechanics which I think differentiate it from other shoot em ups. The first is the magic circle which slows downs green and purple projectiles and clears them from the screen if the enemy shooting them is defeated while the power is active or, alternatively, turns them into more dangerous homing yellow bullets if the enemy escapes. 
The second one are spells which are consumables sold by the pumpkin sisters whose shop is available 2-3 times per level. Spells are like bombs in other games, clearing projectiles around the player. They also provide a free hit and upgrade the player's weapon for a brief period of time.
I think both mechanics combined incentivize the player to be more aggressive in general in contrast to other shoot em ups where it's more efficient to focus almost purely on dodging. Boss fights also lack time limits and with the right timing it's possible to trivialize some phases. 
Obviously the art style is very characterizing of the title as well, every single sprite is clear and colorful, and the tone is generally lighthearted. Each playable character comes with a fully voiced story mode, but the english translation is hilariously bad. It's around the same "engrish" level as the store description. 
Overall, I believe the game is pretty good. I don't think it's the best shoot them up for a newcomer, but there's an easy mode and infinite credits so it's not the worst either. I did get a bit sick from the over the top voice acting though.

[h1]Un solido Bullet Hell...[/h1]
...que hay que aprender a reconocer las diferencias entre Bullet hell (también llamado Danmaku) y Shoot em up; en genero son casi igual pero no en especie; a resumidas cuentas: Bullet hell= balas y lucecitas a lo pendej0 en pantalla, a veces ojo a veces te dan una habilidad para salvaguardarte; Shoot em up= tienes Power ups(por lo general), tu bombita y la curva de dificultad va subiendo, sin llenar toda la pantalla de lucecitas de caca; en ambos manejamos una "navecita", en ambos hay buena música y escenarios y en ambos casi siempre tenemos que salvar al mundo, o pelear vs un "mal mayor" así que este título es menester decirlo es un bullet hell.

>A Grandes Rasgos:
Pues ya explicado de estos jueguitos, este titulo es un bullet hell decente en el que manejamos a unas brujitas, todas con sus propias historias, tipo de disparo y pet, con su propio lore y objetivos dentro del juego, que en general con todas es "pelear" vs otras hechiceras por X o Y causa.
  
Sus "mecánicas" propias son que tenemos un "escudito" que paraliza proyectiles y los convierte en moneditas después de un tiempo, mismas que puedes utilizar para comprar 3 tipos de "hechizos" de un solo uso entre misiones en una tienda muy a la fantasy zone, lo que te hará plantearte como utilizaras estas "cartitas" y en qué momento, ya que de igual forma es preciso decirlo este bullet hell no es tan misericorde, es un bullet hell para los que les gustan los bullet hell xD así que advertido quedas del título.

>Lo Bueno:
+Todo el titulo tiene actuación de voz y está bien ilustrado, lo que es de reconocer.
+El gameplay si se diferencia entre brujitas, dentro de lo razonable.
+Tiene cromitos.
+El twist de tener una tiendita de power ups; aunque se vuelve más un bullet hell tactico con esto.

>Lo Meh:
+-La banda sonora, es promedio en realidad; no molesta, ni es excelsa.
+-Las historias... son autistas, pero se entiende, si estas acostumbrado al contenido asiático y su autismo, no tendrás problema.

>Lo Malo:
-esta mal optimizado en cuanto a la relación de aspecto: si tratas de modificar esta te puede crashear o freezear, de igual manera si minimizas el título, lo perderás como tu fe en pensionarte algún día.
-Podría ser (para los que no estén acostumbrados a la longevidad de estos títulos)... la duración, que es el promedio de los títulos de este género: máximo 1 hora te tomara terminar este jueguito... lo que le da replay son los personajes jugables, retos y dificultades.

[h1]Resumiendo[/h1]
Pues... es un sólido bullet hell 6/10 aunque esto lo digo con el sesgo de ser amante de estos títulos... ya que este no es tan misericorde... salvo las dificultades no vas a tener ayudas en el título, es como el promedio del género: aprende a jugar el titulo y sube tu escore... hasta que seas un dios y no te maten y prueba nuevas dificultades... así que; si no eres asiduo consumidor de bullet hells... no te lo recomendaría tanto (hay bullet hells mas amigables), y si vienes por un shoot em up, mejor busca otro título.

ショットボタンを離さないとゴールドが回収出来ないので、
プレイに集中出来ない。
マジックサークルはボタンでオンオフ切り替えなので、
いちいちボタンを押さねばならないのが手間になるので、
ボタンを押している時だけ展開する方式も選べるようにして欲しい。

ボタンはショット、マジックサークル、カード。
ショットは押しっぱなしでオートだが、ゴールド自動回収はショットボタンを離す必要がある。
マジックサークルは、MPがある分だけ展開出来て、敵弾低速化、発射した敵を倒した場合はゴールド変換をする。
カードは、ショップで購入したウェポンを発動する。発動中は１回だけバリアの役割もする。

惜しいと思います。
ゴールドは自動回収で良いと思う。
マジックサークルも、トグル方式ではなくて、押した時にだけ発動する方式で良いと思う。
この操作の手間に気を取られて、ゲームに集中出来ないんですよね・・・。

この２点を変更可能に出来るなら、途端に凄く面白くなると思います。
